rachel_tao: opened PR to tighten wording on the nova-lite model card and catalog: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4921
rachel_tao: Plan: clarify sequence limits, add a concise throughput row with hardware (GPU, batch, seq), swap SDK examples to Async v4 streaming, and call out CPU fallback affect for quant variants. quick sanity check please.
sam_lin: skimmed. card currently lists technical max 8192 but bench CSV is at 4096. we should avoid implying validated sustained 8k.
sophie_docs: suggested wording: "runtime technical max: 8192 (not validated for sustained high-throughput); recommended production ceiling: 4096 for latency-sensitive workloads." add KV-cache note: "KV cache memory grows O(seq_len) 2D enable prefix-caching for repeated contexts."
rachel_tao: current snippet (blocking): ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model="nova-lite", prompt="Summarize...", max_tokens=100)
print(resp.text)
```
rachel_tao: will replace with Async v4 streaming + param rename: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
async with client.stream_generate(model="nova-lite", prompt="Summarize...", max_new_tokens=100) as stream:
    async for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```
sophie_docs: also add short line under limits: "If CPU fallback is used for quantized builds, expect slower cold-starts and ~2-4x lower steady throughput." keep it concise.
bench-bot: PR references bench CSV s3://redwood-bench/nova-lite/2026-04-12.csv - CI link-check will flag if not mirrored.
